gates.question: Does the operation involve surface coating (the application of coating to a substrate) of plastic parts or products?
gates.test: yes: operation falls within the PPPP source category (surface coating of plastic parts and products); no: PPPP source-category gate not met
gates.quote: Surface coating is the application of coating to a substrate using, for example, spray guns or dip tanks. When application of coating to a substrate occurs, then surface coating also includes associated activities, such as surface preparation, cleaning, mixing, and storage.

gates.question: Is the solvent welding step part of a 'coating operation' (i.e., the point at which a given quantity of coating or cleaning material is applied and subsequent points where organic HAP are emitted)?
gates.test: yes: the solvent welding step is part of the affected source and covered as a coating operation; no: the step may not be within the affected source definition for PPPP
gates.quote: but always includes at least the point at which a given quantity of coating or cleaning material is applied to a given part and all subsequent points in the affected source where organic HAP are emitted

gates.question: Is the facility a major source of HAP (any single HAP ≥ 9.07 Mg (10 tons)/yr or any combination of HAP ≥ 22.68 Mg (25 tons)/yr)?
gates.test: yes: facility meets the major-source criterion referenced in PPPP; no: facility is area/source-level and PPPP applicability may differ
gates.quote: A major source of HAP emissions is any stationary source or group of stationary sources located within a contiguous area and under common control that emits or has the potential to emit any single HAP at a rate of 9.07 megagrams (Mg) (10 tons) or more per year or any combination of HAP at a rate of 22.68 Mg (25 tons) or more per year.

gates.question: Does the affected source use 378 liters (100 gallons) per year or more of coatings that contain hazardous air pollutants in the surface coating of plastic parts and products?
gates.test: yes: the 100-gallon-per-year material-use threshold is met and PPPP may apply; no: below the threshold and PPPP may not apply based on that criterion
gates.quote: that uses 378 liters (100 gallons (gal)) per year, or more, of coatings that contain hazardous air pollutants (HAP) in the surface coating of plastic parts and products;

gates.question: Does the operation meet any exclusion in § 63.4481(c) (e.g., the facility uses only coatings, thinners, additives, and cleaning materials that contain no organic HAP)?

gates.quote: A coating operation conducted at a facility where the facility uses only coatings, thinners and other additives, and cleaning materials that contain no organic HAP, as determined according to § 63.3941(a).

gates.question: Is the affected source new or reconstructed (i.e., subject to the new/reconstructed affected-source provisions)?

gates.quote: Affected source means each new or existing ore crushing and handling operation, ore dryer, indurating furnace, or finished pellet handling operation, at your taconite iron ore processing plant.

gates.question: Are the dynamic wet scrubbers in question applied to meet any particulate matter emission limit in Table 1 to Subpart RRRRR?
gates.test: Yes -> the dynamic wet scrubbers are an affected control device under this subpart; No -> these specific provisions for dynamic wet scrubbers in this subpart do not apply
gates.quote: for each dynamic wet scrubber applied to meet any particulate matter emission limit in table 1 to this subpart, you must maintain the daily average scrubber water flow rate and either the daily average fan amperage (a surrogate for fan speed as revolutions per minute) or the daily average pressure drop

gates.question: Did you (or will you) perform an initial particulate matter performance test measuring and recording scrubber water flow rate and either fan amperage or pressure drop every 15 minutes during each test run (to establish site-specific operating limits)?
gates.test: Yes -> operating limits must be established per the test results; No -> you must perform the required performance testing to establish limits before relying on parametric limits
gates.quote: using the CPMS required in § 63.9631(b), measure and record the scrubber water flow rate and either the fan amperage or pressure drop every 15 minutes during each run of the particulate matter performance test.

gates.question: Did the affected source commence construction or reconstruction on or before September 25, 2019 (i.e., is the pre-September 25, 2019 compliance timeline relevant)?
gates.test: Yes -> the provisions with the January 28, 2022 transition date and the earlier option to use either fan amperage or pressure drop apply; No -> post-dates provisions requiring fan amperage (and other timelines) apply
gates.quote: On or before January 28, 2022, for affected sources that commenced construction or reconstruction on or before September 25, 2019, for each dynamic wet scrubber ... you must maintain the daily average scrubber water flow rate and either the daily average fan amperage or the daily average pressure drop at or above the minimum levels established during the initial performance test.

missing: Whether the dynamic wet scrubbers are being used specifically to meet a Table 1 particulate matter emission limit (affirmation of Table 1 applicability); results of the initial PM performance test (the measured fan amperage and/or pressure drop and scrubber water flow rate averages from each run); whether a CPMS was installed and collecting 15-minute data during the performance test; the facility's construction/reconstruction date relative to Sept 25, 2019; which parametric (fan amperage versus pressure drop) was used to establish the operating limit during the initial test.

candidates.title: Kraft/Soda Recovery Furnaces and Related Units (Subpart MM)

gates.question: Is your unit a kraft or soda recovery furnace, smelt dissolving tank, or lime kiln (i.e., the source categories addressed in Subpart MM)?
gates.test: Yes -> Subpart MM monitoring and parameter-setting provisions may apply to dynamic scrubbers on those units; No -> Subpart MM likely does not apply
gates.quote: The owner or operator of each affected kraft or soda recovery furnace or lime kiln equipped with an ESP must install, calibrate, maintain, and operate a COMS in accordance with Performance Specification 1 (PS-1) in appendix B to 40 CFR part 60

gates.question: Is the dynamic wet scrubber a smelt dissolving tank dynamic scrubber operating at ambient pressure or a low-energy entrainment scrubber where the fan speed does not vary (so that fan amperage/PFLA methods are allowed)?
gates.test: Yes -> Subpart MM explicitly allows fan amperage or PFLA methods for those dynamic scrubbers; No -> the PFLA/fan-amperage alternative in Subpart MM does not apply
gates.quote: As an alternative to pressure drop measurement under paragraph (e)(10)(i) of this section, a monitoring device for measurement of fan amperage or fan revolutions per minute (RPM) may be used for smelt dissolving tank dynamic scrubbers that operate at ambient pressure or for low-energy entrainment scrubbers where the fan speed does not vary.

gates.question: Do you intend to set the minimum percent full load amperage (PFLA) to the fan motor using the no-load-plus-10-percent method described in this section?
gates.test: Yes -> the PFLA (no-load percent plus 10%) method is described here as an allowed way to set the minimum fan amperage; No -> you would need to use other allowed methods (e.g., midpoint method or RPM)
gates.quote: The minimum percent full load amperage (PFLA) to the fan motor must be set as the percent of full load amperage under no-load, plus 10 percent.

missing: Whether the dynamic scrubbers are associated with kraft/soda recovery, smelt dissolving tank, lime kiln, or related units covered by Subpart MM; whether the scrubber is the specific low-energy/ambient-pressure type for which fan-amperage/PFLA methods are allowed; manufacturer no-load amperage or a performed no-load test result; the highest 1-hour average fan amperage values from compliant performance test runs (needed to compute PFLA).

gates.question: Have you established site-specific operating limits by measuring pressure drop and scrubber water flow rate at least every 15 minutes during each run of the PM performance test (per the test procedures of this subpart)?

gates.quote: Using the continuous parameter monitoring system (CPMS) required in § 63.9920, measure and record the pressure drop and scrubber water flow rate at least every 15 minutes during each run of the particulate matter performance test.

gates.question: Are your primer-surfacer and topcoat operations part of the covered coating operations under Subpart IIII (automobile and light‑duty truck assembly/paint shop)?
gates.test: yes -> Subpart IIII procedures apply (use Subpart IIII rules to evaluate reuse of prior tests); no -> Subpart IIII may not apply and these gates may not be relevant
gates.quote: To demonstrate initial compliance, the organic HAP emissions from the combined electrodeposition primer, primer-surfacer, topcoat, final repair, glass bonding primer, and glass bonding adhesive operations

gates.question: Was the previous transfer efficiency test conducted using the methods and conditions specified in this subpart?
gates.test: yes -> previous test may qualify for reuse subject to other conditions and approval; no -> you must perform a new transfer efficiency test
gates.quote: Any such previous tests must meet the conditions described in paragraphs (c)(1) through (3) of this section. The previous test must have been conducted using the methods and conditions specified in this subpart.

gates.question: Have there been no process or equipment changes since the December 2004 test?
gates.test: yes -> supports use of the previous test results; no -> you must either demonstrate that the previous results remain reliable despite changes or perform a new test
gates.quote: Either no process or equipment changes have been made since the previous test was performed or the owner or operator must be able to demonstrate that the results of the performance test reliably demonstrate compliance despite process or equipment changes.

gates.question: Did the previous test establish the required operating parameters or collect sufficient data to establish them?
gates.test: yes -> previous test may be acceptable to establish operating limits; no -> you must conduct a new test to establish operating parameters
gates.quote: Either the required operating parameters were established in the previous test or sufficient data were collected in the previous test to establish the required operating parameters.

gates.question: Do you have the test report and supporting calculations/documentation (e.g., panel test report and conversion calculations) required to document a capture/transfer efficiency determination?
gates.test: yes -> you can submit documentation to the Administrator to request approval to use the previous results; no -> lack of documentation will likely require a new test
gates.quote: Records needed to document a capture efficiency determination using a panel test as described in § 63.3165(e) and (g), including a copy of the test report and calculations performed to convert the panel test results to percent capture efficiency values.

gates.question: Have you received approval from the Administrator to use the results of the previous transfer efficiency test instead of conducting a new initial test?
gates.test: yes -> you may use the previous transfer efficiency test results in lieu of a new initial test; no -> you must request approval or perform a new test if other criteria are not met
gates.quote: You are not required to conduct an initial test to determine transfer efficiency if you receive approval to use the results of a test that has been previously conducted.

gates.question: Was the previous test conducted under representative operating conditions (i.e., not during SSM or malfunction) per the performance test requirements?
gates.test: yes -> supports that the prior test is representative and may be acceptable; no -> tests conducted during SSM/nonrepresentative conditions are not acceptable and a new test is needed
gates.quote: You must conduct the performance test under representative operating conditions for the coating operation. Before January 5, 2021, operations during periods of SSM, and during periods of nonoperation do not constitute representative conditions.
